vocabulary.meaning_en: the organ that pumps blood; also your feelings
one of the five parts at the end of your foot
the middle joint of your arm
vocabulary.example: Don't put your elbows on the table.
There was grease all over the pan.

vocabulary.note_ar: لها معنى آخر كفعل: يختبئ / يُخفي.
vocabulary.note_en: As a verb, 'hide' means to go or put something where nobody can see it.
vocabulary.example: The bag is made of cow hide.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to rise up; (of a horse) to stand on its back legs
vocabulary.note_ar: rear كاسم تعني الخلف: the rear of the bus.
vocabulary.note_en: As a noun, 'rear' means the back part: the rear of the bus.
vocabulary.example: The horse reared when it heard the noise.

vocabulary.meaning_en: in a clear way that leaves no doubt
comments that say what is bad about something
vocabulary.example: He listened to the criticism calmly.

vocabulary.meaning_en: comments about how well you did something
vocabulary.example: My teacher gave me useful feedback.

vocabulary.meaning_en: unhappy or worried because of something
vocabulary.example: She was upset after the argument.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to rub something to make it shine
vocabulary.example: He polished his shoes for the interview.

vocabulary.meaning_en: physical or mental energy used to do something
vocabulary.example: Cleaning the garage took a lot of effort.

vocabulary.meaning_en: thinking about something all the time
money you pay to live in a place
vocabulary.example: The rent for this flat is high.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a long time with no rain

fine_lines.title: take something to heart vs live rent-free in your head
fine_lines.explanation_ar: take something to heart: تتأثر بكلام أو نقد وتأخذه بجدية فتحزن. live rent-free in your head: لا تستطيع التوقف عن التفكير في شيء أو شخص، سواء أحببته أو أزعجك.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Take something to heart' means you become upset because you take criticism personally. 'Live rent-free in your head' means you can't stop thinking about something or someone.

examples.sentence: Don't take his joke to heart.
That silly advert lives rent-free in my head.

fine_lines.title: hide vs hair
fine_lines.explanation_ar: في التعبير not see hide nor hair of someone: hide = جلد الحيوان و hair = الشعر، أي «لم أرَ أي أثر له». لاحظ استخدام nor بعد not.
fine_lines.explanation_en: In 'not see hide nor hair of someone', 'hide' is animal skin and 'hair' is hair: you have seen no sign of the person at all. Note 'nor' after 'not'.

examples.sentence: We haven't seen hide nor hair of him all week.
The cold wind made my hair stand on end.

expressions.meaning_ar: يتأثر بالنقد أو الكلام ويأخذه بجدية شخصية فيحزن
expressions.meaning_en: to be upset because you take criticism or advice very personally and seriously
expressions.example: Try not to take the coach's comments to heart – he says that to everyone.

expressions.meaning_ar: يتدخل في عمل أو مسؤولية شخص آخر فيضايقه
expressions.meaning_en: to upset someone by doing something that is their job or responsibility
expressions.example: I don't want to tread on your toes, but can I help with the timetable?

expressions.meaning_ar: جهد بدني كبير، خصوصاً في التنظيف
expressions.meaning_en: hard physical work, often to clean something
expressions.example: With a bit of elbow grease, the old bike looked new again.

expressions.phrase: not see hide nor hair of someone
expressions.meaning_ar: لم يرَ له أي أثر منذ مدة
expressions.meaning_en: to not see someone anywhere for some time
expressions.example: I haven't seen hide nor hair of my neighbour since Monday.

expressions.meaning_ar: تظهر مشكلة أو شيء سيئ من جديد
expressions.meaning_en: when a problem appears or appears again
expressions.example: Just when we finished, the old computer problem reared its ugly head.
Our class won the quiz hands down.

expressions.phrase: make your hair stand on end
expressions.example: The strange noise in the night made my hair stand on end.

expressions.meaning_ar: يشغل تفكيرك باستمرار ولا تستطيع نسيانه
expressions.meaning_en: to be something you cannot stop thinking about
expressions.example: That mistake in the exam has been living rent-free in my head all week.

grammar.title: Idioms with someone / something / one's
grammar.explanation_ar: في القواميس تُكتب التعابير بكلمات عامة مثل someone وsomething وone's. عند الاستخدام نضع الاسم أو الضمير المناسب: tread on someone's toes → tread on my toes / tread on the manager's toes، take something to heart → take it to heart / take his words to heart.
grammar.explanation_en: Dictionaries write idioms with general words like 'someone', 'something' and 'one's'. When you use them, put in the real person or thing: tread on someone's toes → tread on my toes. Take something to heart → take it to heart.
examples: I didn't want to tread on her toes.
That advert lives rent-free in his head.

questions.question: 'You'll win hands down.' What does it mean?
choices: You will win with your hands.
questions.explanation_en: 'Win hands down' means to win easily.

questions.question: Cleaning that oven will need a lot of ___.
questions.explanation_ar: elbow grease = جهد بدني كبير في التنظيف.
questions.explanation_en: 'Elbow grease' is hard physical work, often cleaning.

questions.question: What does 'take something to heart' mean?
questions.explanation_ar: take something to heart = يتأثر بالنقد ويحزن.
questions.explanation_en: It means to be upset because you take criticism personally.

questions.question: 'I haven't seen hide nor hair of Sam.' This means...
choices: I haven't seen Sam anywhere for a while.
questions.explanation_ar: not see hide nor hair = لم أرَ له أي أثر.
questions.explanation_en: It means you haven't seen the person at all for some time.

questions.question: Complete: 'The old problem reared its ugly ___ again.'
questions.explanation_ar: التعبير هو rear its ugly head.

questions.question: If you do someone else's job without asking, you might ___.
choices: make their hair stand on end
questions.explanation_ar: tread on someone's toes = يتدخل في مسؤولية غيره.
questions.explanation_en: 'Tread on someone's toes' means to do something that is their job and upset them.

questions.question: Which situation might make your hair stand on end?
choices: hearing footsteps in an empty house at night
questions.explanation_en: The idiom is about being very frightened.

questions.question: 'That advert lives rent-free in my head.' What does the speaker mean?
choices: I can't stop thinking about the advert.
questions.explanation_ar: live rent-free in your head = يشغل تفكيرك باستمرار.
questions.explanation_en: It means you can't stop thinking about it.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
choices: I haven't seen hide nor hair of him.
I haven't seen hide or hairs of him.
I didn't saw hide nor hair of him.
I haven't seen hair nor hide from him.
questions.explanation_ar: الصيغة الصحيحة: not seen hide nor hair of someone.
questions.explanation_en: The fixed form is 'not seen hide nor hair of someone'.

questions.question: Which idiom is about something you can't stop thinking about?
questions.explanation_ar: live rent-free in your head هو التعبير الصحيح.
questions.explanation_en: 'Live rent-free in your head' is about constant thoughts.
